summary:
Visitors in Nouvelle-Aquitaine stand under the framework of France: rules on identity documents, anti-discrimination law, criminal law and marriage law apply to this region as to every other, and the national oversight mechanisms operate here without regional variation. No transgender finding specific to Nouvelle-Aquitaine was identified in the source inventory.

Prison placement in the region follows the national rule: under Article D248 of the French Criminal Procedure Code men and women are held in separate establishments, so trans women whose legal gender is marked male are placed in men's facilities. A BuzzFeed News feature of 12 January 2018 records a detainee recalling inmates shouting 'We don't want any women here!' and threats of violence. Adeline Hazan, controller-general of places of deprivation of liberty, states that transgender detainees, overwhelmingly women, are the group that suffers the most in prison.
tangentialFactors: The source inventory contains no regional comparison data for Nouvelle-Aquitaine against other French regions on transgender-specific incidents, enforcement, or services.
localsOnly: Residents of Nouvelle-Aquitaine are subject to the same national prison-placement framework, anti-discrimination machinery, and identity-document rules as residents elsewhere in France; no regional variation in these was identified.
outOfScopeNotes: Whether Article D248 placement practice or the CGLPL's 2021 findings have produced measurable change in Nouvelle-Aquitaine's own establishments is unresolved in the source inventory. No regional detention, border, or service-provider data for Nouvelle-Aquitaine was sourced.
